sentences.text: This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of death of Korolla Yamuna, who is daughter of petitioners No.1 and 2, in a road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the case are as follows:
On 26-02-2024 at about 10.10 a.m., the deceased Korolla Yamuna was pillion rider on the scooter bearing Reg. No.KA-01-E-8792, the same being ridden by her father slowly and cautiously, by following all traffic rules and regulations, by wearing headguard and by observing the moving vehicles on the said road, on Jeevanbhimanagar main road.

When they reached near Jeevanbhimanagar bus-stop,
at that time a goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-59-4086, driven by its driver with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner, endangering to human life, came from behind and dashed against the scooter of the deceased.
Due to the said impact, the deceased fell down and sustained grievous injuries.

Immediately after the accident,
she was taken to CMH Hospital, wherein the doctor examined her and declared dead,
while on the way to hospital.
Earlier to the accident, the deceased was LKG student at NSVK Holy Mother English Primary and High School, Jeevanbhimanagar.

sentences.text: She was the only daughter to the petitioners and they had high hope on her.
Due to untimely death of the deceased, the petitioners are mentally shocked, sustained unbearable pain and lost the love and affection.
The Hennur Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said goods vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 304(A) of I.P.C.
The respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.

Therefore, it is prayed to allow the petition and award compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- with interest at the rate of 9%
per annum.

Further it is contended that, the vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-59-4086 is not at all involved in the accident and it was intentionally implicated in collusion with the driver, owner and other authorities to get the unlawful benefit from the insurance company.

There was no rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the goods vehicle, the rider of the TP bike riding the same unmindfully and without observing the traffic and hence the deceased and rider of the bike were the main architect for the unfortunate accident and hence this respondent is not liable to pay any compensation and the petition is liable to be dismissed.

12. At the outset, it is pertinent to note that, in the present case, the date, time and place of accident,
involvement of offending goods vehicle bearing No.KA-59-4086 in the said accident, issuance of insurance policy by the respondent No.2 in respect of said vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident, are not in dispute.

Further, the above oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners has remained undisputed by the owner of offending vehicle/Respondent No.1, as he did not choose to file his written statement and contest the case of the petitioner.

Whereas, the respondent No.2 insurance company has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the scooter bearing No.KA- 01-ER-8792 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of goods vehicle bearing No.KA-59-4086.
But, the respondent No.2 has failed to prove the said contentions.

Except the self serving statements of R.W.1, who is the representative/Legal Manager of respondent No.2, there is no other corroborative oral or documentary evidence placed on record by the respondent No.2 to show that, the said accident has taken place solely due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.
No.KA-01-ER-8792 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of goods vehicle bearing Reg. No.KA-59-4086.

On the other hand, the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, the said accident has taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending goods vehicle bearing No.KA-59-4086 and the deceased Korolla Yamuna has sustained grievous injuries in the said accident and succumbed to said injuries on the way to the hospital.

Though, the learned counsel for respondent No.2 has cross- examined P.W.1 in length, nothing worth has been brought out from his mouth which creates doubt on the veracity of his evidence or establishes that, the said accident has not occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending goods vehicle or there was any negligence on the part of the rider of the scooter.

13. Further, the Ex.P.4 spot mahazar and Ex.P.5 sketch also clearly speaks that, the said accident has occurred on the left side of 30 feet wide road, near Jeevanbhimanagar Bus-stop, Jeevanbhimanagar main road, Bengaluru, in between the offending goods vehicle bearing No.KA-59-4086 and motorcycle bearing No.KA-01-ER-8792 of the deceased.
Further, as per the Motor Vehicle Accident Reports, which are marked as Ex.P.7 and 8, the accident has not taken place due to any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident.

When the accident is not caused due to the any mechanical defects in the vehicles involved in the accident and there was no negligence on the part of the deceased, then in the present facts and circumstances of the case, it can be presumed that, the said accident has occurred due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending goods vehicle.

Further, the investigation officer in his Ex.P.13 final report/charge-sheet has clearly stated that, the accident in question is taken place due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending goods vehicle bearing No.KA-59- 4086.
Admittedly, the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged by the owner or the driver of offending vehicle.

In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the final report of the investigation officer and other police records, regarding the date, time and place of accident, involvement of the offending vehicle, rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle, injuries caused to the deceased in the said accident and cause of Korolla Kristappa Allias Koralla ... vs Ramesh on 6 March, 2026 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/62839735/

sentences.text: Further, the Ex.P.9 post-mortem report, clearly speaks that, the deceased Korolla Yamuna has died due to respiratory failure as a result of injury to lungs and its complications, sustained in the road traffic accident.
There is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the above medical records of the deceased.

In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners, regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending goods vehicle bearing No.KA-59-4086 and cause of death of deceased Korolla Yamuna.

15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court, in the case of Parameshwari V/s Amir Chand and others, reported in (2011)
11 SCC 635, has clearly held that, "in a road accident claim cases the strict principle of proof as in a criminal case are not required."

near Jeevanbhimanagar Bus Stop, Jeevanbhimanagar main road, Bengaluru, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending goods vehicle bearing No.KA-59-4086.
Hence, I answer Issue No.1 in Affirmative.

The said documents clearly goes to show that, the petitioners No.1 and 2 are the parents of deceased Korolla Yamuna.
The relationship of petitioners with the deceased is not specifically denied by the respondent No.2.
Even there is no rebuttal evidence on record with respect to same.
In such circumstances, there is no impediment to believe the above documents produced by the petitioners and hold that, the petitioners are the legal heirs of deceased Korolla Yamuna.

20. The petitioners have asserted that, the age of deceased as on the date of accident was 5 years.

To substantiate the same, the petitioners have produced the Aadhar card of deceased Korolla Yamuna,

Admittedly, as the deceased was a minor, aged about 6 years, as on the date of accident, the question of establishing the avocation and income of the deceased by the petitioners does not arise.

21. As per the latest judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, in M.F.A. No.11440/2011 C/W M.F.A. Ltd., Bengaluru and another, a ready reckoner of the sums payable to a single parent as well as both parents who has/have lost a minor child aged below 15 years of age in a motor vehicle accident for an accident occurring in each year from 1994 till date is provided in Tables 3.1 and 3.2.

22. Accordingly, in the present case, as the deceased was a minor, aged about 6 years, having both parents/father and mother and the accident has taken place in the year 2024 and no medical bills have been produced by the petitioners, compensation amount of Rs.18,76,433/-, is to be awarded to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is held that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.18,76,433/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.
23. Liability:
Admittedly, as on the date of accident the respondent No.1 is the owner and respondent No.2 is the insurer of offending goods vehicle bearing No.KA-59-4086.

As per Ex.R.2 insurance policy bearing No.2315/70658353/00/000, issued by the respondent No.2,
in respect of offending goods vehicle bearing No.KA-59- 4086, was valid from 07-07-2023 to 06-07-2024.
As such, the said policy was valid as on the date of accident i.e. 26-02- 2024.

The evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-59-4086 the said accident has occurred and the deceased has succumbed to grievous injuries sustained in the said accident.
In such circumstances, the respondent No.1 being the owner of said vehicle is vicariously liable to compensate for the damage caused by the said vehicle.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.

On the other hand, the learned counsel for petitioners vehemently argued that, it is settled principle of law that, even if there is a fundamental breach of any condition recognised under Sec.149(2) of Motor vehicles Act, the insurance company is liable to pay the third party and recover the same from the insured.

27. As rightly argued by the learned counsel for the respondent No.2, as per the Ex.P.13 final report/charge- sheet, at the time accident the driver of offending goods vehicle bearing No.KA-59-4086 was not holding driving licence to drive the said vehicle and hence in addition to the offence punishable under Sec. 279 and 304(A) of IPC, he has been charge-sheeted for offence punishable U/Sec. 3(1) R/w 181 of Motor Vehicles Act and the owner of the offending vehicle has been charge-sheeted for the offence punishable under Section 5 R/w 180 of Motor Vehicles Act and admittedly the said final report/charge-sheet has not been challenged either by the driver or the owner offending vehicle.

Further it is pertinent to note that, the respondent No.1 in her Ex.P.11 reply to notice issued under Sec.133 of Motor Vehicles Act has clearly stated that, as on the date of accident the driver of his vehicle was not holding driving licence to drive the said vehicle.
Even, the respondent No.1 did not choose to contest the case of the petitioners.

Therefore, in such circumstances, the respondent No.1 cannot be permitted to take the benefit of his wrong and the respondent No.2/Insurance Company is entitled to raise a defence under Sec.149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.

ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.

The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.18,76,433/- (Rupees eighteen lakh seventy six thousand four hundred and thirty three only), with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioners.

However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order and recover the same from the respondent No.1, in the very proceedings by filing an execution petition.

The above compensation amount is apportioned as follows:
Petitioner No.1 - Father - 50% Petitioner No.2 - Mother - 50% Out of total compensation amount awarded in favour of petitioners No.1 and 2, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in their names as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in their favour, through e-payment on proper identification and verification.

opennyai_summary.facts:
This is petition filed under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988, seeking compensation of Rs.10,00,000/- from the respondents, on account of death of Korolla Yamuna, who is daughter of petitioners No.1 and 2, in a road traffic accident.
The Hennur Traffic Police have registered the case against the driver of the said goods vehicle for the offences punishable under Section 279 and 304(A) of I.P.C.
Hence, they are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the petitioner.
It has contended that, the driver of the vehicle was not having valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
The accused is charge-sheeted under Section 3(1) r/w Section 181 of Motor Vehicles Act along with the owner of the vehicle who was charge-sheeted and the vehicle bearing No.KA-59-4086 was used in a public place without having a valid permit and fitness certificate.
opennyai_summary.issue:
Whether the petitioner proves that, deceased Korolla Yamuna D/o Korolla Kristappa @ Koralla Krishnappa, has succumbed to the injuries sustained in road traffic accident, alleged to have been occurred on 26-02-2024 at about 10.10 a.m.,
near Jeevanbhimanagar bus stop, Jeevanbhimanagar main road, Bengaluru, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Goods Vehicle bearing Reg.
No.KA-59- 4086 ?
2. Whether the petitioner is entitled to compensation?
If so, what is the quantum and from whom ?
3.
What order or Award ?
6.
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
Whereas, the respondent No.2 insurance company has specifically denied the above averred facts and circumstances of the accident and taken specific defence that, the accident has occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the scooter bearing No.KA- 01-ER-8792 and there was no negligence on the part of the driver of goods vehicle bearing No.KA-59-4086.
Further, the Ex.P.9 post-mortem report, clearly speaks that, the deceased Korolla Yamuna has died due to respiratory failure as a result of injury to lungs and its complications, sustained in the road traffic accident.
There is no contrary or rebuttal evidence on record to disbelieve the above medical records of the deceased.
In such circumstances and in the light of above observations, it can safely be held that, the respondents have failed to rebut the oral and documentary evidence placed on record by the petitioners, regarding the rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending goods vehicle bearing No.KA-59-4086 and cause of death of deceased Korolla Yamuna.
15. Further, it is well settled principle of law that, in a case relating to the Motor Accident Claims,
the claimants are not required to prove the case as required to be done in a criminal trial.
The relationship of petitioners with the deceased is not specifically denied by the respondent No.2.
In order to determine the compensation, the age, avocation, income,
dependency, future prospects of the deceased and other conventional heads are to be ascertained.
Admittedly, the accident has taken place on 26-02-2024.
This clearly establishes that, as on the date of accident the age of the deceased was about 6 years.
Admittedly, as the deceased was a minor, aged about 6 years, as on the date of accident, the question of establishing the avocation and income of the deceased by the petitioners does not arise.
The evidence placed on record by the petitioners clearly establishes that, due to rash and negligent driving of the driver of offending vehicle bearing Reg. No. KA-59-4086 the said accident has occurred and the deceased has succumbed to grievous injuries sustained in the said accident.
The respondent No.2 being the insurer of the vehicle has to indemnify the respondent No.1.
In such circumstances,
the burden was on the respondent No.1 to establish that, as on the date of accident the driver of his vehicle was holding valid & effective driving licence to drive the offending vehicle, which he has failed to discharge in the present case, as he did not choose to file his written statement and contest the case of the petitioners.
Even, the respondent No.1 did not choose to contest the case of the petitioners.
Therefore, in such circumstances, the respondent No.1 cannot be permitted to take the benefit of his wrong and the respondent No.2/Insurance Company is entitled to raise a defence under Sec.149(2) of Motor Vehicles Act.
opennyai_summary.decision:
22. Accordingly, in the present case, as the deceased was a minor, aged about 6 years, having both parents/father and mother and the accident has taken place in the year 2024 and no medical bills have been produced by the petitioners, compensation amount of Rs.18,76,433/-, is to be awarded to the petitioners.
Therefore, it is held that, the petitioners are entitled for total compensation of Rs.18,76,433/-, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum, from the date of petition till its realization.
Following the aforesaid decisions, we deem it appropriate to allow the appeal by directing that the first respondent (i.e. the insurer) shall satisfy the award, though, however, it can recover the amount so paid from the insured (i.e. owner of the vehicle)".
However, the primary liability is on the respondent No.2 to pay the compensation to the petitioners and later recover the same from the respondent No.1.
Accordingly, it is held that, the respondent No.2 is liable to pay the above compensation of Rs.18,76,433/- to the petitioners, with interest at the rate of 6% per annum,
from the date of petition till its realization and recover the same from the respondent No.1.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 in Partly Affirmative.
30. Issue No.3:
In view of the above findings, I proceed to pass the following order:
ORDER
The petition is partly allowed with costs.
The petitioners are entitled for compensation of Rs.18,76,433/- (Rupees eighteen lakh seventy six thousand four hundred and thirty three only), with interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of petition till realisation.
The respondents No.1 & 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the above compensation amount to the petitioners.
However, the primary liability to pay the compensation amount is fastened on respondent No.2 - Insurance Company and it is directed to pay the said amount within two months from the date of this order and recover the same from the respondent No.1, in the very proceedings by filing an execution petition.
The above compensation amount is apportioned as follows:
Petitioner No.1 - Father - 50% Petitioner No.2 - Mother - 50% Out of total compensation amount awarded in favour of petitioners No.1 and 2, 30% of the compensation amount with proportionate interest shall be deposited in their names as fixed deposit in any nationalized bank for the period of three years with liberty to draw the accrued interest periodically and the remaining 70% amount with proportionate interest shall be released in their favour, through e-payment on proper identification and verification.
9 Advocate's fee is fixed at Rs.2,000/-.
Draw award accordingly.
